alignments.note: Third-person imperative rendered by the support frame 'Let ... be in subjection'; rule 17 heads on the meaning-bearing complement 'subjection' rather than on the auxiliary 'Let' or the copula 'be'. Discontinuity permitted by rule 15.

Anarthrous dative noun: no Greek article competes, so under rule 58 the supplied determiner belongs to the noun and the case preposition 'to' rides with it, as 'μόνῳ θεῷ' → 'to the only God'. Discontinuous under rule 15.
Attributive participle rendered by the bare adjective 'higher'; the determiner is the noun's under rule 58.
Expressed existential verb with the supplied expletive subject 'there' as a rule 7 helper; head on the verb word.

The negator takes the single English negative determiner 'no'. Rules 41 and 59 do not empty it: 'ἐξουσία' is not itself a negative word, and rule 87's construction (a universal πᾶς with a negator) is not present here.
Noun; the negation is the negator's own word.
εἰ μή rendered by the single word 'but' is one indivisible unit under rule 39, headed on the first particle and on the English word.

Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 splits the phrase, and under rule 102 the article takes both the determiner and the supplied nominal 'powers', headed on the nominal. Rule 103 confirms the fold even though 'powers' echoes t010, because the supplied noun stands inside the phrase this article governs.
The participle carries the relativizer and the finite English verb under rule 32.
Expressed copula of the periphrastic perfect passive; the participle is a separate source token and keeps its own word.

review_notes: Both variant units are underdetermined with the base reading compatible; no textual decision is made inside the alignment (rule 12).

s014 could alternatively be given a bare pronoun with 'powers' marked added under rule 103, but rule 103 says in terms that a supplied nominal inside a Greek article's own phrase is folded there under rule 102.
